docs.summary: Connects two navmesh positions that aren't walkably connected — a jump over a gap, a drop off a ledge, a ladder. Agents whose area mask includes [`Area`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink~Area) traverse it as part of pathing; the crowd animates the hop and manual traversal is not supported. Links are BAKED data, kept beside the layers and re-injected whenever a tile is re-contoured, so carving and links coexist; with [`AutoRebuild`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink~AutoRebuild) on this component rebuilds the tiles around its endpoints when it changes. Traversal cost comes from the area's cost, so price a link by giving it its own area. Enabled outside play too, because a bake gathers links from the registry only enabled links are in.
Toggling this rebuilds the affected tiles in place.

Which surfaces the link resolves against is part of its definition: narrowing the scope has to rebuild the surfaces it is coming off, which is why this applies like an edit. Edits made to the set in place are picked up on the next frame.

Persistent id stamped on the baked connections, resolving a traversing agent back to this component ([`CurrentOffMeshLinkData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshAgent~CurrentOffMeshLinkData)). Derived from the component's [`Identifier`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Component~Identifier), which the scene persists, so it survives a reload and a duplicated object gets its own. Resolution is best-effort — baked data can outlive the component that produced it — so don't hang gameplay-critical logic on `CurrentOffMeshLinkData.Link`.
Does this link apply to bakes for the given agent type?
This link as a self-contained bake payload (world space, current state).
Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.
Called every frame after all Update functions have been called.

Draws whatever the navmesh made of this link — the same connection the surface's overlay draws, in the same place, so the two agree wherever both are shown. A link that has not attached has nothing there to draw, so it falls back to the authored line in grey: that difference in colour is the only warning that it reached nothing walkable.
